requirements.evidence: All contract routes in routes/web.php:18-42 with correct names/methods/middleware (throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed on verification.verify, guest group for login/register, auth+verified on home). Login.php:28-56 validates strictly, throttles per lowercase email+IP with auth.throttle, auth.failed on email, regenerates session, redirectIntended(route('home')). Register.php:30-62 uses key str()->transliterate('register|'.$ip), 5 attempts, error on email, fires Registered, logs in, regenerates. PasswordResetController.php:52-76 rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset; sendLink always flashes passwords.sent. EmailVerificationController.php:32-48 checks id+hash against the logged-in user (403 otherwise); send() redirects verified users home without sending. User implements MustVerifyEmail; Password::defaults() in AppServiceProvider; .env.example, phpunit.xml locale pins and lang/{en,pt_BR}/ui.php present; reset view has a single name="email" input.

conventions.evidence: Login uses #[Validate] + $this->validate() (Login.php:16-20); views use route() and an anonymous <x-form-field> component; plain wire:model; CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md updated; PHPDoc on public methods. Deviations: Register.php:72-79 uses a rules() method instead of the project's #[Validate] pattern; User::create in Register.php:51 is a write done inline rather than via app/Actions (debatable for auth); docs/business-rules.md:75 claims 'Forms are throttled to 6 requests per minute' but password.update has no throttle.

security.evidence: Verification link bound to the logged-in user with hash_equals (EmailVerificationController.php:36-40); forgot password never reveals accounts; logout invalidates and regenerates token; login/register refuse to act for an authenticated session (Login.php:30, Register.php:32); rate limits inside Livewire methods; {{ }} escaping everywhere; #[Fillable] unchanged and remember_token set via forceFill. Gaps with limited impact: POST /reset-password (routes/web.php:32) is not throttled; layout loads Bulma from a third-party CDN without SRI as a fallback (components/layouts/app.blade.php:12).

tests.evidence: Pest feature tests for every requirement: LoginTest (pt_BR/en rendering, intended redirect, remember cookie, auth.failed, strict email, 5-try lockout with exact throttle message, auth-switch attempt), RegisterTest (confirmed rule, default password rule, unique, limiter key, throttle on email, authenticated-user tamper), EmailVerificationTest (tampered id 403 verifying nobody, wrong hash, unsigned, guests, resend/verified resend, 429), ForgotPasswordTest (same status for unknown e-mail, 7th request 429), ResetPasswordTest (single email input, remember_token rotation, event), LogoutTest, HomeTest, LocalizationTest, PasswordRuleTest, ViewConventionsTest.

simplicity.evidence: Lean controllers using Password broker and framework events directly; shared <x-form-field> removes duplicated markup; no service layers. Minor extra: the CDN fallback branch in the layout (components/layouts/app.blade.php:10-14) is speculative.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names (throttleKey, sendLink, resetPassword), purposeful comments (Register.php:46 explains counting every submit), consistent Bulma markup across views, no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task; config/app.php default locale change is consistent with it. The third-party CDN stylesheet fallback in the layout (app.blade.php:12) is an unrequested addition touching asset loading.

issues.explanation: POST /reset-password (password.update) has no throttle, so token/password attempts on the reset endpoint are not rate limited, while docs claim the forms are throttled.
Docs state 'Forms are throttled to 6 requests per minute' for password reset, but only the forgot-password POST is throttled, so docs and code disagree.
Register validates via a rules() method instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern used in Login and named in conventions.
Layout falls back to loading Bulma from cdn.jsdelivr.net without Subresource Integrity, an unrequested third-party dependency.
User creation is done inline in the component rather than through an app/Actions class; acceptable for auth but diverges from the 'writes go through Actions' convention.

review.summary: The change implements the full session auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, home, forgot/reset password, own-account e-mail verification) with pt_BR-first translations, Password::defaults(), and a thorough Pest suite covering throttling, tampering and localization. Remaining issues are small: the reset POST is not throttled despite the docs saying so, Register uses rules() rather than #[Validate], and the layout adds an unrequested CDN fallback; approvable with minor fixes.
